item.title: Agents struggle with the same bad UX we do (7 minute read)
item.description: Computer-use AI agents frequently fail at the same confusing interfaces that frustrate humans, including ambiguous buttons, hidden menus, unexplained disabled states, and disruptive overlays. People often compensate for these problems by guessing, backtracking, or relying on experience, while agents expose the underlying design debt through repeatable failures that are easier to observe. Making interfaces clearer for agents through explicit labels, visible states, predictable interactions, and semantic structure can also improve accessibility and usability for people.

item.title: Everyone is building AI agents. Who's designing the stop button? (17 minute read)
item.description: AI agents introduce unpredictable behavior into products traditionally designed around explicit rules and known transitions, making it essential to distinguish where autonomy is useful from where reliability is mandatory. Products can let AI interpret intentions and construct workflows while using deterministic execution, visible uncertainty, confirmation steps, and clear recovery mechanisms to protect consequential actions. Designing effective agent experiences increasingly means defining boundaries around what AI may decide, when humans must intervene, and how users can understand, correct, or stop an autonomous process.

item.title: Why 10,000 experiments work better than 10,000 hours for designers (6 minute read)
item.description: Repeatedly practicing the same design skills can make someone better at their current job without developing the problem-framing, influence, and decision-making abilities required for more senior roles. Instead of relying on experience alone, designers can break career goals into microskills and run small experiments, such as opening every design review with a specific decision or presenting research findings themselves. A weekly reflection can help turn these experiments into deliberate professional growth without requiring organizational approval or major changes to existing workflows.

item.title: Tokenizer Mono (30 minute read)

Most styles achieve roughly 98% agreement with real tokenizers in testing, demonstrating how advanced font technology can perform surprisingly complex text processing while revealing its limitations around line breaks, uncommon words, and tokenization algorithms.

item.title: Philippine Migrant Worker Data Likely Leaked in 69GB Breach (3 minute read)

item.title: Finding 40+ Vulnerabilities in Healthcare Software Serving More Than 100 Million Patients (13 minute read)

The issues include three critical findings: local file disclosure through the PDF generator, SQL injection through patient-data field names, and another SQL injection. Other bugs exposed patient records, allowed portal credential replacement, and enabled administrator API impersonation through an impersonation chain that combined SQL injection and file disclosure to forge an OAuth bearer token, bypassing password and MFA checks.

item.title: Why Conventional Reputation Feeds Miss Software Supply Chain Attacks (18 minute read)
item.description: Conventional threat intelligence feeds and multi-engine scanners fail to detect most software supply chain attacks on day zero, exposing organizations to malicious package behavior for months after public disclosure. Research indicates that blind-spot rates for supply chain attacks in these reputation tools range from 70% to 90%. General-purpose security tools remain ineffective against these threats because they are designed to detect inbound perimeter probes rather than malicious package behavior.

item.title: You Had Me at “Hello”: Inside The Greeter, A Chinese‑Language Framework Targeting AI Infrastructure (15 minute read)
item.description: Era researchers tracked a Chinese-language framework, Greeter, exploiting Flowise's overrideConfig code-injection flaw (CVE-2024-58351) across seven honeypots from July to October. Each “hello” request delivered a different command through javascriptFunction, without changing the saved chatflow. The framework ran host reconnaissance, searched .env files, SSH keys, and Flowise encryption keys, probed AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud metadata services, and checked Docker socket access, Linux capabilities, persistence paths, and memory-based execution. Of 3,277 identifiable internet-exposed Flowise instances, 703 lacked authentication. 46 matched the honeypot's vulnerable conditions.

item.title: Prioritize What Attackers Will Exploit: 4 Elements of Strong Exposure Prioritization (7 minute read)
item.description: Fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are exploited, but remediation programs often treat most findings as urgent. item.title: The Quiet Phase: Why Active Directory Group Enumeration Deserves Your Attention (9 minute read)
item.description: Attackers map who sits in Domain Admins with SharpHound or PowerView long before they change any group membership, and an audit entry (SACL) on the group's member attribute turns those reads into Event 4662, or 4799 for built-in groups, on the domain controller that answered. On real privileged groups, the signal drowns in reads from directory sync, Exchange, and admin tooling, and SAMR-based tools like net group /domain bypass it entirely. Pair the audit with decoy groups that nothing legitimate ever reads, correlate a decoy read and a real admin-group read from the same logon session, and check coverage with its QuietPhase PowerShell script.

item.title: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time (11 minute read)
item.description: A Renault Latitude's TomTom Carminat LIVE head unit hid its clock settings behind a legitimate navigation SD card. The author reverse-engineered the Linux 2.6.28 firmware, built a QEMU and CAN emulator, and found that master.script allowed a root path-traversal write through its LOG command and wrote |/bin/sh /media/sdcard/payload.sh into /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern, then crashed /bin/dbus-monitor to trigger a coredump and execute the payload as root. The exploit enabled an eMMC backup and a timezone patch from UTC+3 to UTC+2.

item.title: The hidden latency inside your database (7 minute read)

item.title: Resisting Cognitive Surrender (12 minute read)

item.title: Discovering a Backdoor and Flaws in More Encrypted USB Drives (10 minute read)
item.description: Vector 35 researcher Xusheng Li pointed Codex at Binary Ninja's MCP server and recovered the keys hardcoded in NetacFileLock, KakaSoft USB Copy Protection, and Nexcopy Copy Secure in 7 to 26 minutes each. In each product, the key was fixed in the binary, derived from an embedded seed, or unlocked by a certificate in the viewer, so the user's password never protected the files. Separately, time-travel debugging turned up two hidden accounts in SecZure's YutianDun drive, with passwords as weak as "123456", that could decrypt any file. Li skipped vendor disclosure because drives already in the field can't be patched, and he argued that client-side validation is never secure, so buyers should only trust drives that derive their encryption key from the user's password.

item.title: Agentic Offensive Frameworks Hit Real Intrusions (34 minute read)

ARTEX users included financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters such as UNC7228, which went from a first account to deep access in about four hours, though GTIG noted the agents were forensically noisy and sometimes undid each other's work. Mandiant recommended short-lived, tightly scoped credentials, locking down admin interfaces like Kudu/SCM as privileged infrastructure, and behavioral detection tuned for machine-speed bursts.

item.title: CVE-2026-98432: which Linux kernels are still vulnerable (5 minute read)
item.description: Mattias Geniar found 712 Multipath TCP listeners on his own Ubuntu 26.04 laptop, opened without his knowledge by Go programs like tailscaled, because Go 1.24 and later enable MPTCP on listening sockets by default. That matters because the only known exploit for CVE-2026-98432 needs an MPTCP listener. The bug is a use-after-free in the kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake that dates back to Linux 4.4 and can be reached with a single SYN. Upstream stable kernels were fixed in mid-October, and Debian, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK have shipped patches, but Ubuntu and RHEL still had no fixed kernel as of November 1.

item.title: Securing Internet-Critical Software: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash (7 minute read)
item.description: GNU Savannah's Savane forge passed a user's email address unescaped into a shell command during GPG key testing, so an RFC-valid address containing backtick-wrapped commands gave any registered user code execution on the backend. Hacktron researchers used that foothold to read database credentials, grant themselves superuser, and impersonate Bash maintainer Chet Ramey, which exposed an SSH key page that would have allowed pushes to upstream Bash, before an unpatched GameOver(lay) kernel bug gave them root and a key to a GNU backup server. The FSF fixed all 26 reported flaws, and forge operators should pass process arguments as arrays rather than shell strings, treat email local parts as untrusted input, and verify that LTS kernels actually receive backported fixes.

item.title: Threat Hunting for Malicious IP-KVM Usage (7 minute read)
item.description: IP-KVM devices like PiKVM let remote operators drive a machine at the hardware layer with input indistinguishable from a local user, a tactic North Korean IT workers used to control laptop farms. Nebulock's hunt guide treated its sparse-peripheral and onboarding-timing heuristics as triage signals rather than attribution, since product strings and VID/PIDs can be spoofed. Threat hunters should search USB telemetry for known KVM vendors, then flag rare composite HID devices that also expose storage, networking, or video, and correlate hits with new-hire timing and identity anomalies before escalating to physical inspection.

item.title: Designing for People with ADHD (9 minute read)
item.description: ADHD affects about 5% of people and stems from differences in how the brain develops focus, planning, and self-regulation. It is not a matter of willpower. ADHD often overlaps with autism, dyslexia, and anxiety, so designing for it tends to help several groups at once.

item.title: One size doesn't fit all: rethinking “good design” across cultures (9 minute read)
item.description: Ideas such as clarity, simplicity, restraint, and functionality are often treated as universal measures of good design even though they emerged from particular Western histories and cultural contexts. Design traditions excluded from the dominant canon can use decoration, complexity, symbolism, and craft in ways that are deeply functional within their cultures, challenging assumptions that minimalism is inherently more sophisticated or understandable. Evaluating design more broadly requires asking who established prevailing standards of taste, whose histories were documented and taught, and whether a design successfully serves its specific cultural purpose rather than conforming to a supposedly universal aesthetic.

item.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth (7 minute read)
item.description: A 16-year-old buffer overflow in TianoCore EDK2's PXE Base Code driver (CVE-2026-97631, CVSS 9.5), the reference UEFI code behind most server firmware, allowed an attacker to send an oversized ICMP error during network boot and execute ring 0 code before Secure Boot and the TPM chain of trust loaded. An AMI pull request leaked the fix months ahead of a January coordinated disclosure, although exploitation required local network access and per-model address tuning. Defenders should request patched firmware from their UEFI vendors, disable PXE boot where feasible, and monitor network boot segments for anomalous ICMP traffic.

item.title: 3 design principles in the AI age (5 minute read)
item.description: Three enduring principles remain essential to good design despite AI dramatically accelerating creative work: iteration, feedback, and connecting the dots. Faster generation makes exploring alternatives cheaper, but quality still requires repeated refinement, diverse human perspectives, and judgment about which feedback matters rather than accepting AI's first answer or treating it as the only critic. Designers also need time away from production to process accumulated knowledge and recognize larger connections, because AI can generate faster than humans can meaningfully reflect.

item.title: Design as a garden (2 minute read)

Pruning unnecessary work and deliberately leaving room for play can be as important as producing more, while not every experiment needs an obvious payoff. Ideas also benefit from periods of inactivity and patience, making it useful to distinguish between moments that require greater effort and those that simply require more time.

item.description: Oxygen is adding a setting that lets KDE users choose between symbolic and colorful action icons, but supporting that seemingly simple preference requires redrawing hundreds of icons individually at multiple sizes. Different pixel dimensions require distinct proportions and levels of detail rather than straightforward scaling, turning one interface option into thousands of assets that must be designed, tested, and maintained. User choice carries a substantial hidden cost, but removing choice also has consequences when people have different visual preferences, habits, and accessibility needs.

item.title: Conran Design Group rebrands luxury accommodation provider Cheval (4 minute read)
item.description: Conran Design Group has repositioned luxury accommodation provider Cheval around “Generous by design,” shifting the brand from a product-led proposition toward experiences defined by space, time, and attention. A new elongated C containing two horses references Cheval's Knightsbridge origins, while Season typography, deep teal, bespoke property emblems, and flag-inspired signage replace more generic black, white, and gold luxury conventions. The flexible identity supports Cheval's expansion across serviced apartments and branded residences while giving individual properties room to express their distinct locations and character.

item.title: Masani Pizza's identity celebrates the family that owns it (5 minute read)
item.description: Saint-Urbain built Masani Pizza's identity around the personality and family behind the restaurant, giving the brand a warm, characterful presence rather than relying on familiar Italian restaurant conventions. Expressive typography, illustrations, photography, and playful graphic details create a visual language that feels personal and rooted in the people running the business. The resulting system turns family character and hospitality into the restaurant's primary point of distinction across packaging, signage, merchandise, and other touchpoints.

item.title: Hackers Claim 590GB PwC Data Theft (2 minute read)
item.description: The Everest extortion group claims to have stolen 590GB of data from PwC, including HR and regional training data exports, integration documents, software components, and eLearning materials. The attackers claim that the data includes names, employment history, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses. PwC acknowledged the breach but stated that the affected site did not store client info, personal data, or financial information.

item.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles (5 minute read)
item.description: Attackers wielding stolen GitHub tokens from more than 850 accounts planted over 13,500 "sync-check" workflows that base32-encode repository and environment secrets to evade log masking, then pulled the logs through GitHub's own API and deleted the runs. GitHub's approval hold blocked every public-repository run, but private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server executed the payload, with a newer variant sweeping self-hosted runners for cloud, Kubernetes, and AI provider credentials. Defenders should hunt for ci-sync-* branches, the gheist user agent, and OIDC role assumptions from those branches, then rotate every secret an affected repository could reach, since deleting the branch does not undo the exposure.

item.title: Critical HTTP2Shell Brotli Vulnerability Triggers Emergency Patches (2 minute read)
item.description: Originally reported as a Node.js vulnerability, researchers found that a critical flaw in the Brotli decoder could affect software across multiple ecosystems that use it. The vulnerability stems from a buffer overflow that an attacker can exploit with a specially crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Node.js, .NET, and several Python libraries released emergency patches to fix the vulnerability.

item.title: Security Assessment Report — Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5 (48 minute read)
item.description: Researchers report verified flaws in Tailscale v1.104.2 and headscale v0.29.5. Tailscale SSH Unix-socket forwarding runs as root, enabling privilege escalation, socket replacement, root-file deletion, enrollment-key theft, and rogue node enrollment. The experimental conn25 connector lets an entitled user reach cloud metadata, internal LANs, and Kubernetes services without destination validation. Headscale has unauthenticated memory-exhaustion and onboarding-lockout issues. Recommended controls include per-pair SSH grants, forwarding disabled, connector egress allowlists, hardware-bound credentials, and control-plane node deletion during incident response.

item.title: How LLM-Based Penetration Testing Harnesses Work (16 minute read)
item.description: Utku Sen tested three open-source LLM penetration-testing harnesses - Cairn, Artex, and Strix - against a deliberately vulnerable e-commerce site containing DOM XSS, unpaid purchases, IDOR, and account takeover. A harness turns model output into real actions: reading files, running commands, browsing, and using tools such as Nmap, Nuclei, Katana, and Playwright. Cairn pursued single goals through planner and worker agents. Artex, linked by CrowdStrike to attacks on South Korean finance targets, used its own agent library and found all vulnerabilities except account takeover. Strix added reconnaissance, defined vulnerability classes, and produced a structured report. Sen found that a Pi harness using DeepSeek with a simple goal prompt found the account-takeover flaw and outperformed Cairn.

item.title: How the Claude Code Team Does Code Review (14 minute read)
item.description: To account for the number of changes being made, Anthropic shifted to a model where Claude Code serves as the primary code reviewer, with most PRs requiring at most one human in the loop. Developers run tests, builds, and lints, etc., locally before opening a PR. Every PR runs standard CI checks, plus a security and bug review. A classifier then determines whether zero, one, or two reviewers are needed before the change enters a merge queue, and changes are rolled out internally via feature flags before reaching a public release. Anthropic uses data from incidents as well as metrics from PRs to evaluate and tune their reviewer agents.

item.title: Who do you trust when you trust a certificate? The eMudhra incident explained (12 minute read)
item.description: One of eight compromised eMudhra intermediate CA private keys was literally the number 4, the result of a flawed April 2025 key ceremony that left the top 376 bits of every key zeroed. Browsers blocked the intermediates within hours through OneCRL, CRLSets, and Certificate Transparency checks, but Python, Go, Node, Java, and curl skipped revocation entirely and kept trusting forged chains until their bundled trust stores changed. The fixes split along architecture lines, with certifi, Debian, and uv dropping the entire emSign G3 root while Go and Node denylisted only the eight broken keys, sparing roughly 30,000 legitimate certificates.

item.title: UK Biobank back online soon, months after someone tried to sell 500k people's data on Alibaba (3 minute read)
item.description: UK Biobank says its Research Analysis Platform is secure and will reopen after government approval. The April attack led to data for all 500,000 volunteers being listed for sale on Alibaba. Access will return in phases: manual file review before downloads, no result downloads initially, 15-minute idle logouts with 2FA, isolated browsing, SSH removal, and CLI limits. Researchers must remove de-identified participant data from code repositories before regaining access.

item.title: uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts (4 minute read)
item.description: The uCreator Android spyware kit hides inside sideloaded Telegram and Telegram X builds or runs WeChat in its own container. It can read chats, capture Telegram 2FA passwords before hashing, reset sessions, change phone numbers, and hide attacker devices. Its WeChat module extracts login credentials and clones accounts. A leaked backend shows a rentable service with customer IDs, phone farms, bulk-contact operations, and scheduled activity designed to evade platform risk checks.
